# Zephyrium Docs

> Documentation for Zephyrium, a privacy-preserving layer-1 chain with the ZEP coin.

This file contains links to documentation sections following the llmstxt.org standard.

## Table of Contents

- [Concepts](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/get-started/concepts): What Zephyrium keeps private, how the chain is structured, and its current limits.
- [Quick start](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/get-started/quick-start): Build, launch and check a local Zephyrium devnet.
- [ZEP Documentation](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/): Run a node, validate, and build on the Zephyrium privacy chain.
- [pDEX](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/pdex): The exchange built into the Zephyrium chain.
- [pTokens](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/ptokens): Private tokens on Zephyrium.
- [pWallet](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/products/pwallet): The browser-extension wallet for Zephyrium.
- [Changelog](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/changelog): What Zephyrium has changed, by date.
- [License](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/license): Zephyrium is open-source software under the MIT License.
- [Roadmap](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/resources/roadmap): The Zephyrium roadmap is being finalised and will be published soon.
- [ZEP tokenomics](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/tokenomics/zep): The ZEP supply cap, who receives it, and the 21-year release schedule.
- [Network parameters](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/network-parameters): Every devnet setting and where it lives.
- [Node types](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/node-types): The four kinds of node, what each does and what it needs.
- [Validators and rewards](https://developers.zephyrium.ai/validators/overview): Stake amounts, how a validator gets a seat, and how rewards are split.
